problem: Generative trajectory planners (CVAE/diffusion) produce geometrically feasible, diverse paths but lack semantic understanding to choose among them, while VLM-based Generate-and-Select methods (TGS, MOSU) rely on slow, API-based large models with second-scale latency.
motivation: Outdoor mapless navigation needs both multimodal trajectory proposals (e.g. left or right of a tree) and semantic preferences (pavement over grass) without maintaining global maps. A lightweight open-vocabulary segmenter can supply semantic costs in real time, and decoupling geometry from semantics allows changing behaviour by only changing prompts and costs.
key_idea: Generate 200+ diverse feasible trajectories with a perception-constrained CVAE (NaVAE), score them by projecting onto a CLIPSeg open-vocabulary semantic cost map plus a goal term, and switch trajectories asynchronously with hysteresis.
insight: The ablations show the LME multi-modal loss and collision loss are crucial: with the standard MUSE-VAE loss SR falls to 2/6 and NTR rises to 54.0 (vs 23.8); without the collision loss SR is 2/6 and NTR 43.5. Hysteresis-based asynchronous updates beat fixed-frequency reselection (4/6 vs 6/6, EPT 90.7 vs 94.5). The system is agnostic to the local planner (DWA is similar to RL planner).
method: NaVAE CVAE generator: learned-prior CVAE with a prior encoder (PointNet LiDAR features, goal MLP, state-history LSTM), a BiLSTM posterior encoder and an autoregressive GRU velocity decoder that samples K=200 trajectories of 12 waypoints.

PointNet-constrained decoding: a pre-trained PointNet does binary traversable/non-traversable segmentation of LiDAR, rasterized to a Gaussian-smoothed heatmap used to constrain the decoder and filter sampled velocities (acceleration limit 0.5 m/s^2).
LME training objective: log-mean-exp reconstruction loss for the prior over M valid ground-truth trajectories (soft winner-takes-all, IWAE-like) plus collision loss on GT semantic map and KL term.
Geometric collision filter: 18x18 m elevation map; trajectories are discarded if the pitch between consecutive waypoints exceeds a threshold.

CLIPSeg semantic cost map: off-the-shelf CLIPSeg (~130M) with prompts 'a photo of a [class]', per-pixel argmax mapped to user-defined class costs; trajectories are projected 3D-to-2D onto the image and scored with discounted costs, an occlusion mask and a goal-distance/heading term.

Asynchronous update with hysteresis: the executing trajectory's future waypoints are re-scored at 2.5 Hz while generation runs at 0.5 Hz, and a switch occurs only if the new cost is lower by epsilon; a local planner (RL-based, 50 Hz) executes velocities.

setting.backbone: NaVAE (CVAE + PointNet, trained from scratch) + CLIPSeg base (frozen, off-the-shelf) + RL local planner
setting.training_data: Real-world dataset: 1,706 samples (~8,500 synthetic NavFN candidate trajectories) from 15 teleoperation runs on a university campus; CLIPSeg zero-shot
setting.observation: 64-channel LiDAR point clouds (last 3 frames), robot state history, RGB camera FPV, GPS-derived polar goal
setting.action_space: Generated waypoint trajectories (12 waypoints at 1 s) tracked by a local planner outputting velocity commands
setting.privileged: none at test time (semantic maps, AMCL and NavFN used only for training supervision and offline evaluation)

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 unseen-sector configurations of 120-240 m, 6 repeats each
numbers.extra: Real robot (Husarion Panther UGV); success radius 5 m; metric-mapless; GPS goal
numbers.evidence: Table 'Comparison of baselines and our model': Sem-NaVAE 0.90±0.30, FD 6.02±0.51, EPT 95.0±3.12, NTR 23.4±6.88, Tratio 1.33±0.03, #RB 2±1

numbers.extra: Real robot; SR given as successes out of 6

numbers_note: Custom real-world benchmark; no standard benchmarks. SR in the main table is printed as 0.90 (converted to 90).
results: In real-world outdoor tests on unseen campus routes of 120-240 m, Sem-NaVAE reaches 0.90 SR versus 0.80 for NoMaD, 0.63 for MTG', 0.40 for VL-TGS and 0.17 for MTG, close to the map-based Nav2 (0.97). It is also far faster than the baselines (T_ratio 1.33 vs 2.27-4.12), near Nav2's 1.28, and completed a >1 km GPS-only park run.
limitations: Evaluated only in campus and park environments, without varied weather, adverse lighting or dense pedestrian traffic
Few repeated trials per route, so high variance; ablations use only 6 trials
Semantic costs are hand-defined per class, argmax CLIPSeg is simple and the selection is limited by the 3D-to-2D projection and occlusion; CLIPSeg latency (~400 ms) bounds the update rate
